planting.note: Start seeds indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost, or plant container stock in spring in well-drained, lean soil in full sun; Blue Boy is a compact rue selection with intensely blue-toned foliage.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean, alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; avoid wet or highly fertile soils. CAUTION: handle with gloves, since rue contains furanocoumarins that can cause skin blistering after contact and subsequent sun exposure. Blue Boy is a compact selection of rue with especially vivid blue-gray, finely divided foliage on a tidy, low-mounding plant, smaller and more richly colored than the species, making it a favorite for herb garden edging and formal knot gardens where its striking foliage color is the main attraction. Small yellow flowers appear in summer but the plant is grown primarily for foliage. It serves as a larval host plant for Giant Swallowtail butterfly caterpillars, and its strong scent is reputed to repel a number of garden pests. Cut back after flowering to keep the plant compact and encourage fresh foliage growth.

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost, or plant container stock in spring in well-drained, lean soil in full sun; Curly Girl bears distinctively ruffled, curled blue-green foliage.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean, alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; avoid wet or highly fertile soils. CAUTION: handle with gloves, since rue contains furanocoumarins that can cause skin blistering after contact and subsequent sun exposure. Curly Girl bears distinctively ruffled, tightly curled blue-green foliage on a compact plant, an unusual textural novelty among rue cultivars that makes it a conversation piece in an herb garden or formal edging planting. Like other rue, it is grown mainly as an ornamental and companion plant rather than for culinary use in quantity, since the flavor is intensely bitter. It serves as a larval host plant for Giant Swallowtail butterfly caterpillars, and its strong scent is reputed to repel several garden pests. Cut back after flowering to maintain a tidy, compact form.

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; Oriental Limelight is grown for its bright chartreuse-and-cream variegated foliage rather than for flowers, and it spreads by rhizomes, so give it room or grow it in a container to contain spread.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in partial shade to full sun; some afternoon shade helps preserve the brightest variegation and prevents scorch in hot summer sun. Oriental Limelight bears bold, deeply cut leaves splashed with bright chartreuse-yellow and cream over green, one of the most vividly variegated foliage plants in the artemisia genus, providing strong color contrast in a mixed border throughout the growing season. Unlike ornamental silver-leaved artemisias, it tolerates more shade and moisture, though it still needs decent drainage to avoid root problems. It spreads by rhizomes and can become assertive in good conditions, so site it where its spread is welcome or contain it in a large pot. Cut back hard in late winter to renew growth and remove any plain-green reverted shoots promptly to keep the variegation stable.
